intro: Walter Goehr leads the National Symphony Orchestra of London in a 1945 Kingsway Hall recording. This is Decca K 1321’s first side only; the source does not identify the orchestral arranger.
question: How does Goehr shape the opening before the side continues beyond the comparison?

cues.title: Kingsway Hall, 1945
cues.text: The source names Goehr and the National Symphony Orchestra of London at Kingsway Hall. It dates both recording and first release to 1945, but gives no arranger for the orchestral version.
cues.evidence: Commons distinguishes performers, place, first recording and first release; its arranger entry is “none”, not a reliable identification.

cues.title: A contrast in weight
cues.text: After the opening’s fuller sound, this stretch drops in recorded weight while the surface remains active. Compare that balance with the earlier orchestral phrases, not only with the piano recording’s tone.
cues.evidence: The report falls from −9.3 dB at 1:10 to −22.7 at 1:15 and −24.2 at 1:20, with a 1:12 boundary.

cues.title: Renewed orchestral weight
cues.text: The later continuation returns to stronger recorded weight after a quieter span. Follow the shape of the whole gesture rather than interpreting each change as a separate tempo instruction.
cues.evidence: At the 2:30 boundary relative level rises from −25.2 dB at 2:25 to −11.0 at 2:30 and −10.0 at 2:35.

cues.title: A crest and its aftermath
cues.text: The side’s largest measured crest is followed by a withdrawal. This lies beyond the aligned opening, where differences of version and side extent prevent a whole-file speed comparison.
cues.evidence: The highest window is 3:25 at −8.2 dB; 3:35 falls to −25.4 after the 3:32 boundary. No whole-work comparison is inferred.

composer.background:
Liszt was born in Doborján, a German-speaking village in the Hungarian kingdom, where his father Adam worked on an Esterházy estate. Hungary remained his declared homeland, although German and French were his principal languages. Adam taught him piano before taking him to Vienna in 1822 for lessons with Carl Czerny, who had studied with Beethoven, and Antonio Salieri. The family moved to Paris the following year. The Conservatoire refused him admission as a foreigner; private teaching and public concerts supplied his education instead. His early career therefore joined two institutions that would remain distinct in his adult life: the disciplined lesson and the commercial concert platform.

Adam died in 1827, leaving the sixteen-year-old Liszt to support himself and his mother by teaching. Paris offered an education beyond the keyboard: Victor Hugo, the religious social thinker Félicité de Lamennais, Chopin and Berlioz belonged to his intellectual or musical circle. Hearing Paganini in 1832 suggested that a pianist might make technical difficulty carry the same theatrical force as the violinist’s leaps and harmonics. Liszt responded with prolonged practice and transcription: his piano version of Berlioz’s Symphonie fantastique, published in 1834, aimed to preserve orchestral detail.
composer.born: 22 October 1811, Doborján, Kingdom of Hungary (now Raiding, Austria)
composer.epithet: The touring pianist who made a single theme change character, and eventually stripped virtuosity down to a few unresolved notes.
